name: TV DIABLO Windows
note: v1932: The last unswept class from the gate-hardening brief: a guard that cannot reach its subject, found by measuring the OVERLAP between every name-set the pipeline holds and the roster it is judged against, because the count is the tell. Reading the set-group table properly turned up a real defect: five of its thirty eight keys are PIECE names rather than set names, with a helm keyed as a set carrying two other pieces and a shield carrying two more. The reader grouped rows under a row instead of under the heading. Set groups alone are harmless because no UI reads them, but completeSets is the one that bites - a set the panel calls complete is one row worth five pieces, expanded by the board, so a piece accepted there would tick pieces he does not own from a single misread heading. It has not happened yet, which is exactly when a guard is cheap. The refusal carries its reel and frame and is printed by the sweep, because a silently dropped group is indistinguishable from a page that held none. The guard first cut had the very defect it was written about: it stripped the slot suffix from the roster and compared the raw input, so it caught one spelling and missed the other, and its own test caught it.
